name: astryx
description: An open source design system that's fully customizable and agent ready
readmeHtml:
Astryx

An open source design system that's fully customizable and built for how we build now:
by people and the agents working alongside them.

Currently in Beta · Built on React 19+ and StyleX

Docs · Storybook · Sandbox · Contributing · Discord

Overview

Astryx is an open source design system that grew inside Meta over the last eight years, where it became the most-used and largest design system in the company — powering 13,000+ apps and shaped by the engineers, designers, and product teams who depend on it every day.

It ships 150+ accessible components, brand-level theming, dark mode, ready-to-ship templates, and a CLI as one cohesive system. You import pre-built CSS and use typed React components — no build plugin, no styling library to adopt — and both people and AI assistants build with the same tooling.

What makes Astryx different:

  • Open internals. Components are built to be composed at any level, not locked behind a closed top-level API. The building blocks you'd reach for are exported directly, and when you need to go deeper, swizzle ejects a component's full source into your project to own.
  • No styling lock-in. Astryx authors its styles with StyleX, but that's invisible to consumers. Override with className using Tailwind, CSS modules, or plain CSS — whatever your project already uses.
  • Customize without wrapping. A theme is a set of CSS custom property overrides, so a designer can make Astryx unmistakably theirs without forking or wrapping component source.
  • Built for people and agents. The API, docs, and CLI are designed together so a person and an AI assistant build the same way, from the same reference.

Getting Started

Astryx requires React 19 or later (react and react-dom are peer dependencies of @astryxdesign/core).

Install Astryx, a theme, and its peer dependencies:

# npm
npm install @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex
npm install -D @astryxdesign/cli

# pnpm
pnpm add @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex
pnpm add -D @astryxdesign/cli

# yarn
yarn add @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex
yarn add -D @astryxdesign/cli

Then finish setup with init, once, before you write UI. It asks no questions, prints the getting-started steps (styles, theme), and saves the Astryx guide to AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md so you and your agents build with Astryx instead of guessing:

npx @astryxdesign/cli init   # or: pnpm exec astryx init / yarn astryx init

You can also install the CLI once for your computer, so astryx works in any folder and every coding agent knows Astryx; in a project, it still runs that project's own version:

npm i -g @astryxdesign/cli

Project install, global install, or both? astryx docs global/project-global-or-both compares them (both is recommended), and astryx docs global explains how global mode works.

The simplest setup is a few CSS imports plus a theme provider — no build plugin, no PostCSS or Babel config. See the @astryxdesign/core README for the full guide (Next.js, Tailwind, Vite, and CDN).

For reliable CLI access, add a script to your package.json:

"scripts": {
  "astryx": "node node_modules/@astryxdesign/cli/clients/cli/bin/astryx.mjs"
}

Then use it as npm run astryx -- component --list. This avoids path errors when AI assistants or new developers invoke the CLI directly.

Packages

Package Description README
@astryxdesign/core Components, theme system, and utilities README
@astryxdesign/cli CLI tooling: component docs, templates, scaffolding, themes, and codemods README
@astryxdesign/build Build plugins for StyleX source builds README
@astryxdesign/theme-* Seven ready-made, fully customizable themes (neutral, butter, chocolate, matcha, stone, gothic, y2k) README

@astryxdesign/lab (experimental components) is used internally for Storybook and the sandbox and is not published to npm. @astryxdesign/vega (Vega/Vega-Lite chart wrapper) and @astryxdesign/charts (chart components) are published to npm only under the @canary dist-tag — there is no stable release yet.

Principles

These are the promises Astryx makes to the people building on it.

  • Guidance over enforcement. Components give you capability rather than guardrails that fight you. Design opinions live in docs and examples — if you pass a value, the component renders it.
  • Strong, documented conventions. Every component follows the same naming, prop, and composition rules, and every one is thoroughly documented — so once you've learned a few, the rest feel familiar, and both people and AI can predict how an unfamiliar component behaves.
  • One system for humans and AI. The API, conventions, docs, and CLI are designed together so people and AI assistants build the same way. Every change that made Astryx easier for AI made it easier for people too.
  • Earned by measurement. We test conventions rather than assert them, hold the results loosely, and revisit them when a new situation proves them wrong.

Architecture

Foundations

The building blocks for visually cohesive and accessible interfaces: typography, color, layout, and accessibility.

Components

A library of 150+ reusable UI building blocks with full TypeScript support.

Patterns

Battle-tested design solutions for common interactions and workflows: table pages, detail page layouts, form wizards, navigation patterns, data entry flows.

Project Structure

Directory Purpose
apps/ Example apps, the docsite, and Storybook
packages/ Published packages: core, cli, build, themes
internal/ Internal tooling: test utilities, eslint plugin, vibe tests

Contributing

We welcome contributions! See CONTRIBUTING.md for the full guide.

Questions, or want a hand with a PR? Come find us in Discord.

Our conventions and review rubrics live in the Contributing wiki — including API Conventions, Design Conventions, the Component Lifecycle, the Contributing Templates, and the Blog Review Rubric. Read the relevant rubric before opening a PR.

For local development, install the Node.js version pinned in .nvmrc and use pnpm 11. If you use nvm, run nvm install from the repository root. The CLI package supports Node.js 22.13.0 and later when run in consumer projects.

Install pnpm directly, or enable Corepack so the pinned pnpm version installs automatically:

corepack enable
pnpm install

If corepack is missing, install pnpm directly or install Corepack manually; see the troubleshooting notes in CONTRIBUTING.md.

The Theme Showcase DOM tests use the root ui project for shared DOM and StyleX test setup. Run pnpm exec vitest run --project ui apps/docsite/src/__tests__/theme-showcase/ from the repository root.

License

MIT

releases.name: Astryx v0.7.17
releases.body:
# Astryx v0.7.17

Upgrade every Astryx package your app uses to `0.7.17`, then run:

```bash
astryx upgrade --from 0.7.16 --apply
```

## Highlights

- [`Item` and `ListItem` swipe actions](https://github.com/meta/astryx/pull/8690) now track a finger through the full UIKit-like open, confirm, fire, and cancel motion.
- [`TextInput`, `TextArea`, and `NumberInput`](https://github.com/meta/astryx/pull/9777) stay visible above a phone or tablet keyboard and restore the page or scroll area after it closes.
- [`TopNavMenu` and `TopNavMegaMenu`](https://github.com/meta/astryx/pull/12140) close once after a touch or keyboard selection and return focus to the trigger.
- [`Selector` and `MultiSelector`](https://github.com/meta/astryx/pull/11851) return focus after a selection, while growing option lists keep the selected row aligned with the trigger.
- Core adds touch motion for AlertDialog, safer clipboard fallback in restricted frames, more reliable focus and layer behavior, stronger accessibility states, and smaller initial bundles for optional menus and tooltips.
- The CLI gains one-base routing, MCP tools for every command, faster kept catalogs and upgrade scans, clearer theme and integ

releases.body:
Astryx 0.7.16 — all `@astryxdesign/*` packages ship at this version.

```bash
OLD_VERSION=0.7.15  # replace with the Core version your project uses today
npm install @astryxdesign/core@0.7.16 @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.16  # plus every other @astryxdesign/* package you use, at 0.7.16
npx @astryxdesign/cli upgrade --from "$OLD_VERSION" --apply --path .
```

## @astryxdesign/core

### Experimental APIs

- Adds the English strings of the Lab media player (`@astryx.mediaPlayer.*`): control names, spoken times, chapter and marker context, and previous and next track. They are Lab strings shipped in Core's locale file, as Lab ListInput's strings are; they add no public API to `@astryxdesign/core`. ([#11438](/meta/astryx/pull/11438))

### New Features

- NumberInput takes `entryErrorBehavior`, so a form can pass one value to all of its date, time, and number fields. A typed number is complete only at Enter or blur, so both values keep NumberInput's current timing: its rejection, `aria-invalid`, announcement, and `onEntryErrorChange` report appear at Enter or blur, never while a person types. releases.name: v0.7.15
releases.body:
Astryx 0.7.15 — all `@astryxdesign/*` packages ship at this version.

```bash
OLD_VERSION=0.7.14  # replace with the Core version your project uses today
npm install @astryxdesign/core@0.7.15 @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.15  # plus every other @astryxdesign/* package you use, at 0.7.15
npx @astryxdesign/cli upgrade --from "$OLD_VERSION" --apply --path .
```

## Known issue

In Safari/WebKit with default motion, a tall tooltip can briefly cover its trigger for its first entrance frame before settling beside it. Interaction is unaffected; this is fixed in v0.7.16.

## @astryxdesign/core

### New Features

- DateInput, DateTimeInput: `onEntryErrorChange` reports why the field rejects typed text, so an app can word its own message. It receives a `DateInputEntryError` (exported from both components) with a `kind` that does not depend on the locale (`unreadable`, `incomplete`, `nonexistent`, `outOfRange` for a date before `min` or after `max`, or `unavailable` for a day that `dateConstraints` rules out), the typed `text`, and, for `outOfRange` and `unavailable`, the Gregorian ISO `date`. releases.name: v0.7.14
releases.body:
Astryx 0.7.14 — all `@astryxdesign/*` packages ship at this version.

```bash
OLD_VERSION=0.7.13  # replace with the Core version your project uses today
npm install @astryxdesign/core@0.7.14 @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.14  # plus every other @astryxdesign/* package you use, at 0.7.14
npx @astryxdesign/cli upgrade --from "$OLD_VERSION" --apply --path .
```

## @astryxdesign/core

### New Features

- ComplexSelector: `disabledMessage` explains why a disabled selector is disabled. With `isDisabled`, a tooltip shows the reason on hover and keyboard focus, and the reason describes the trigger through `aria-describedby`. The disabled trigger keeps its tab stop, and pointer, keyboard and the imperative handle still cannot open the popup. With `renderTrigger`, the caller owns the control, and `disabledMessage` works with it too: the tooltip and the description go to that control. Drop the control's own tooltip while the selector is disabled, for example `tooltip={isDisabled ? undefined : 'Filter'}`, so it never shows two. Separately, a caller's own `aria-disabled` now reaches an enabled built-in trigger. (#5984)

releases.name: v0.7.13
releases.body:
Astryx 0.7.13 — all `@astryxdesign/*` packages ship at this version.

```bash
OLD_VERSION=0.7.12  # replace with the Core version your project uses today
npm install @astryxdesign/core@0.7.13 @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.13  # plus every other @astryxdesign/* package you use, at 0.7.13
npx @astryxdesign/cli upgrade --from "$OLD_VERSION" --apply --path .
```

## @astryxdesign/core

### New Features

- Tokenizer forwards BaseTypeahead's `menu` and `onOpenChange` in its inline presentation, and its handle gains `open()` and `close()`. A token whose own button calls `open()` with a dialog-role menu opens the dialog, and Escape returns focus to that token: focus that a press puts on a token's control, and the menu's focus return, stay there instead of moving to the input. The sheet presentation keeps its own sheet. (#10624)

- Typeahead: Backspace or Delete on the selected Token clears the value, as the clear button does, when the clear button shows: it calls `onChange(null)`, announces the cleared value, and moves focus to the empty input. Without `hasClear`, the keys start editing, as a click does. (#10847)

aiSummary.oneLiner: An open-source, customizable design system built on React 19 and StyleX for both human developers and AI agents.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Astryx is a massive open-source design system originating from Meta, engineered to be the foundational UI layer for both human developers and AI assistants. Built on top of React 19 and StyleX, it provides over 150 accessible, ready-to-use components alongside robust brand-level theming and native dark mode support. Unlike traditional design systems, Astryx features open internals that allow components to be composed at any level, and includes a swizzle CLI command to eject source code directly into a project. It explicitly aims to provide unified tooling that AI coding agents can understand and manipulate as effectively as human engineers.
keyFeatures: Extensive component library: Ships with over 150 fully accessible, typed React components ready for production use.
Agent-ready architecture: Designed with predictable patterns and tooling specifically tailored for AI coding assistants to utilize.
Open internals: Allows developers to compose building blocks directly or use the swizzle command to eject raw component source code.
StyleX foundation: Leverages StyleX for highly performant, zero-runtime CSS-in-JS styling without complex build plugins.
Comprehensive theming: Includes robust support for brand-level customization, strict design tokens, and automatic dark mode.

useCases.title: Enterprise application scaling
useCases.description: Standardizing the UI layer across thousands of internal applications using a highly performant and accessible component library.

useCases.title: AI-assisted UI development
useCases.description: Providing an AI coding agent with a predictable design system to rapidly prototype complex interfaces from mockups.

useCases.title: Custom design system foundation
useCases.description: Ejecting base components via the CLI to heavily customize logic and styling for a unique brand identity.

useCases.title: Performance-critical interfaces
useCases.description: Building fast-loading web applications that leverage StyleX's atomic CSS generation for minimal styling overhead.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Frontend engineers, design technologists, and teams building large-scale React applications who want a deeply customizable, AI-friendly design system. It provides a robust foundation for building consistent and performant user interfaces. The agent-ready design ensures that components can be easily manipulated and composed by AI tools.
